title: Admin toolbelt + playbook-to-automation pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Support and SRE teams maintain dozens of manual playbooks for common incidents (KV cache corruption, model skew, capacity failover). These are split between Google Docs, ad-hoc scripts in github/redwood-tools, and chat instructions. Problem: long TTR for incidents, duplicated effort, and risk from manual step mistakes.

Goal: Build a reproducible pipeline that consolidates admin utilities into a single toolbelt (redwood-admin), standardizes playbooks as Linear task templates, and implements a safe automation layer that can execute approved remediation steps with human-in-the-loop checks. The deliverable is a minimal production system that: 1) provides a canonical CLI for guarded admin ops, 2) converts 8 high-priority runbooks into task templates with attached automation hooks, and 3) exposes a runbook-orchestrator service that executes scripted steps (via GitHub Actions or internal runner) when a responder approves.

Scope: MVP covers infra-facing playbooks only (serving runtime, routing, cache invalidation, model fallbacks). Does not include customer-facing data exports or schema-migration automations.

Non-goals: Full self-healing automation or automatic escalation to legal/compliance.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Consolidated CLI vs multiple small scripts: single binary simplifies discoverability and RBAC, but increases blast radius. We will gate destructive commands behind a confirmation API and require SSO-based approval for automated runs.
- Task templates in Linear vs external runbook system: we choose Linear task templates to keep incident state close to workflows and telemetry, at cost of having to implement hooks for automation triggers.
- Execution backend: start with GitHub Actions runners (fast to iterate) and plan a move to internal safe-runner for lower-latency control.

Technical approach:
1) redwood-admin: Go-based CLI with subcommands for safe ops (cache:invalidate, cache:rehydrate, route:switch, model:pin). Includes dry-run mode, structured JSON outputs, and audit headers.
2) Task templates: for each playbook create a Linear template with checklist steps, expected signals, rollback steps, and a single "run automation" link that opens a UI to request execution.
3) Orchestrator: small service with a REST endpoint that validates request signatures, checks RBAC via SSO, and queues a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the requested scripts in a sandbox. The orchestration returns run logs and a verification checklist back to the Linear task.

Acceptance criteria:
- redwood-admin binary available in internal releases and downloadable via downloads.redwood.com/internal.
- 8 production runbooks converted to Linear templates and used in at least 2 on-call incidents during rollout.
- Orchestrator executes a guarded script with approval workflow and writes audit events to CloudAudit and Linear task comments.
- No increased incident MTTR in the first month; target is 20% reduction by month two.

Security and compliance:
- All admin commands require SSO tokens and are logged with requestor identity.
- Secrets never passed in clear; runners pull from runtime KMS using short-lived credentials.
- Security review required prior to any automated execution of destructive steps (field: security_review_required = true).

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): internal CLI prototype and convert 3 low-risk runbooks to templates. Manual-run only.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): build orchestrator + GitHub Actions integration, add approval modal in internal Console. Pilot with SRE on non-prod.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): enable automation for production on low-risk operations, collect metrics, iterate on UI and timeouts.

Monitoring and metrics:
- Track number of automated vs manual steps, time from task creation to completion, and post-action failure rate.
- Audit logs pushed to ELK and sampled to support analytics dashboard in Console.

Open questions:
- Should we allow escalation to PagerDuty from the orchestrator or keep PagerDuty integration within Linear only? (engineering ops preference: keep in Linear for visibility).
- Long-term: migrate to internal runner to reduce secrets surface and latency — timeline TBD.

Attachments/links: See links below for design doc, initial PR, and sample task templates.
